title: Cost vs Value Pricing Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 24
description:
Laddoo Lab sells a six-pack for Rs 120. But where does that number come from? Is it too high, too low, or just right? In this animated lesson Zoya, Arjun and Nani test their price three ways, in a home kitchen in Bengaluru.

You will see cost-based (cost-plus) pricing built live, block by block: ingredients Rs 45, box and label Rs 15, gas and electricity Rs 8 and delivery Rs 12 make a cost of Rs 80, and a 50% markup of Rs 40 gives Rs 120. Then competition-based pricing, with similar snacks nearby at Rs 100, Rs 110 and Rs 130, and value-based pricing, with a survey of ten parents whose answers average Rs 140. We put it together with Kotler and Armstrong's idea that costs set the price floor and customer value sets the ceiling, and see the three methods at work in a furniture maker, two tea stalls and an airline. We also look at the human side honestly: every method has a blind spot, Laddoo Lab leaves a fair gap below value, and in India every pack must print its MRP, inclusive of all taxes, which no shop may exceed. All figures are example figures.

This is Episode 24 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
